chapters.1.summary: The book is called the Song of songs. A woman speaks first and longs for her lover’s kisses. She says his love is better than wine and his name is like perfume. She tells the women of Jerusalem that she is dark and lovely. The sun has darkened her, since her brothers made her tend the vineyards. She asks her lover where he pastures his flock. He praises her beauty and compares her to a fine mare. She says he is like a bundle of myrrh and a cluster of henna.
chapters.2.summary: The woman calls herself a flower of the plain. Her lover says she is a lily among thorns. She says he is an apple tree among the trees of the forest. She asks the women of Jerusalem not to stir up love before its time. She hears him coming, leaping over the hills. He looks through the window and calls her to come away. Winter is past, the flowers appear, and the doves are heard. She says her beloved is hers and she is his.
chapters.3.summary: At night on her bed the woman looks for the one she loves. She does not find him. She gets up and searches the streets and squares. The watchmen find her, and she asks whether they have seen him. Just past them she finds him and holds him. She will not let go until she brings him to her mother’s house. Then a grand procession comes up from the wilderness. It is Solomon’s carriage, guarded by sixty armed men.
chapters.4.summary: The man praises the woman’s beauty part by part. Her eyes are doves, and her hair is like goats on a hillside. Her neck is like a tower hung with shields. One glance from her has captured his heart. Her love is better than wine, and her lips drip honey. He calls her a locked garden and a sealed spring. The garden holds pomegranates, nard, saffron, cinnamon, and myrrh. She calls the winds to blow and invites him into the garden.
chapters.5.summary: The man says he has come into his garden. Then the woman tells of a night when her heart was awake. Her beloved knocked and asked her to open. She had undressed and washed her feet, and she hesitated. When she opened the door, he was gone. She searched and called, and he did not answer. The watchmen found her, beat her, and took her cloak. The women ask what makes him special, and she describes him from head to foot.
chapters.6.summary: The women of Jerusalem ask where her beloved has gone. They offer to look for him with her. She answers that he has gone down to his garden. She says she is his and he is hers. He praises her as beautiful as a great city and awesome as an army. Her eyes overwhelm him. A king may have many queens, but she is his only one. She went down to the orchard to see whether the vines had budded.
chapters.7.summary: The man praises the woman from her feet to her head. Her neck is like an ivory tower, and her eyes are like pools. Her hair holds a king captive. She is like a palm tree, and he will climb it. She says she belongs to her beloved and his desire is for her. She invites him to go out to the fields and stay in the villages. They will rise early to see whether the vines have budded. There she will give him her love.
chapters.8.summary: The woman wishes she could kiss her lover in public without scorn. She asks again that love not be stirred before its time. She asks him to set her as a seal on his heart and arm. Love is as strong as death, and its flame is a mighty fire. Her brothers discuss how to guard their little sister. She answers that she is a wall and has found peace. Solomon rents out a vineyard for silver, but her vineyard is her own. She calls her beloved to hurry like a gazelle.
